decision_reason: A1 describes overall motion well but underrepresents movement distribution and the direction of postural change. Rowing has the weakest reported seen coverage; upper-limb motion and sagittal trunk excursion offer complementary, observable transfer cues. Upper-limb motion also provides a conditional distinction between stepper and cross-trainer exercise. The close flat-versus-inclined treadmill pair does not justify inventing a reliably observable additional distinction from incline alone. Likewise, elevator travel and outdoor-versus-treadmill progression remain imperfectly observable with short-window inertial evidence. Preserve useful A1 concepts and add two scoped dimensions without claiming improved recognition or forcing every class pair apart.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: upper_limb_motion
attributes.definition: Magnitude of active upper-limb movement relative to the torso, distinguishing arm participation from movement transmitted through the whole body.

levels.Low: Arms remain nearly fixed relative to the torso or move only slightly.
levels.Medium: Arms show moderate movement relative to the torso.
levels.High: Arms show pronounced movement relative to the torso.

attributes.name: trunk_pitch_excursion
attributes.definition: Extent of forward-and-backward change in the torso's gravity-relative inclination within a window, excluding isolated limb motion and turning about the upright axis.

levels.Low: Little or no forward-and-backward torso inclination change.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotation magnitude. It preserves a broad transfer cue from vigorous seen exercise to rowing and inclined walking. Pace, technique and individual effort can blur ordinal boundaries; retaining it avoids assuming a new incline-specific signature.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)
contrast_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in arm, leg and torso motion. This transfers cyclic movement structure from seen exercise to walking and rowing without encoding activity identity. Harmonics, multiple moving segments and variable voluntary pace can make the meaningful repetition unit ambiguous.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes in inertial signals. It preserves a transferable contrast between continuous machine exercise and fluctuating stair descent. Movement speed and vibration can affect the evidence; smoothness alone does not justify separating the two lying postures.
contrast_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: impulsiveness: G10 supports brief abrupt changes associated with impacts. Seen jumping supplies an impact anchor for descending stairs, while non-impact exercise supplies the opposite pattern. Foot placement and equipment transients can blur levels; elevator start or stop events are not guaranteed to occur in a window.

posture_inclination: G1 supports mean gravity-relative orientation across torso and leg sensors. Upright, seated and reclined seen configurations provide broad posture anchors for unseen activities. Global load-bearing posture is not identical to torso lean, and treadmill slope does not prescribe a fixed body inclination.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)
contrast_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in horizontal positions

operations.reason: posture_variability: G12 supports changes in gravity-relative body configuration. It retains a broad distinction between stable standing, locomotion and substantial postural movement, providing seen support for rowing. Dynamic acceleration can obscure gravity estimates, and limb motion must not be mistaken for global posture change.
contrast_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: rotational_motion: G2 supports angular movement across the available body segments. Cyclic leg rotation and whole-body angular activity remain transferable anchors for unseen walking and rowing. The aggregate concept does not identify which segment rotates, motivating a separate upper-limb dimension rather than changing this definition.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translational-motion evidence, preserving the physical distinction between progression and stationary exercise. Ascending stairs provides a locomotor anchor for descent and outdoor walking. Constant-velocity elevator travel, long-term displacement and treadmill-versus-overground location are not reliably established by these proxies; no extra travel-direction attribute is added.
contrast_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: motion_regularity: G11 and G6 support recurrence and temporal predictability. Structured seen exercise and less structured elevator movement provide transferable anchors for treadmill walking, rowing and outdoor walking. Window duration, pauses and voluntary pacing can blur differences; outdoor walking is not necessarily irregular.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: upper_limb_motion: G2 and G3 support arm angular motion and movement magnitude, with torso observations helping distinguish active arm movement from whole-body carriage. This supplies rowing with a transferable arm-participation cue from cross-trainer exercise and basketball, beyond overall intensity. It can also supplement the one-coordinate A1 stepper-versus-cross-trainer contrast when moving handles are used. Handle use, hand support and rowing technique are unspecified, so separation is conditional rather than guaranteed; relative motion requires adequate segment alignment.
contrast_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: trunk_pitch_excursion: G12 supports torso gravity-angle variation and G2 supports forward-and-backward angular movement. Rowing commonly includes trunk rocking, supplying a directional postural cue beyond aggregate rotation and limb-dominated exercise; standing and relatively stable-torso exercise anchor low excursion, while basketball offers variable trunk movement. This is a scoped extent, not an assumed rowing rhythm or joint angle. Technique, restricted trunk use, dynamic acceleration and anatomical-plane alignment can reduce predictability, and no seen activity is assumed to reproduce a rowing stroke.
contrast_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

semantic_redundancy_review: The eleven dimensions distinguish total magnitude, repetition rate, sustained roughness, isolated impacts, mean posture, global posture change, overall rotation, progression, predictability, arm participation and sagittal torso excursion. Upper-limb motion localizes activity that overall intensity and rotation cannot localize. Trunk pitch excursion partially overlaps posture variability but restricts the evidence to forward-backward torso motion rather than arbitrary global reconfiguration; it also differs from mean inclination. Smoothness and impulsiveness retain sustained-versus-transient meanings, and cadence remains separate from regularity. All A1 inputs and A2 outputs are accounted for once. No extra distinction is imposed for flat versus inclined treadmill walking, stationary standing versus steady elevator travel, or the two lying postures where a new split-specific, reliably transferable dimension is not justified.
